description: Per-world display names for party jobs: struktured's own evolution table, docs/job_evolutions_by_world.md (his commits 2026-03-08/09). Archetype in W1, individual from W2, essence by W6. The novellas and cutscene prose use these same names.
_canon_restored: 2026-11-05 (cowir-story, at cowir-main's go): this table replaced an AI-authored set (Mall Cop, Stoker, Ward Matron, Floor Boss…) that no human chose, which 0 lines of novella or cutscene prose used while the doc names appear there hundreds of times. A veto of any cell is a one-line change here.
_source: struktured, TYPED turn 2026-03-21T02:44:41Z (V3 Pass plan): 'characters should be referred to by class title only (Fighter, Cleric, Mage, Rogue, Bard and their per-world evolution names)'. His phrase is 'per-world evolution names' and his list is exactly these five jobs, which is where _scope comes from.
_attribution_correction: An earlier version of this field quoted him as asking on 2026-08-09 for names to change per overworld, with 'Fighter -> Mall Cop' as HIS example. Neither is sourceable. A sweep of every transcript on this box found ZERO typed user turns containing 'Mall Cop'; its earliest occurrence anywhere is my own W2 spotlight-duel design text of 2026-07-01, describing the miniboss w2_fighter_mall_captain. Those AI-authored names were replaced 2026-11-05 by his own table (_canon_restored); the names below are his.
_key_on: GameState.current_world (int 1-6), NOT a map id and NOT a world word. It is set at one chokepoint (GameLoop._set_current_map_id) and is already corrected for shared interiors: inn/shop/quest-room ids carry no world prefix, so _get_world_for_map() alone returns 1 for them and _village_origin_id is what fixes it. Calling _get_world_for_map(current_map_id) directly gives medieval names in every W2-W6 shop while the overworld outside shows the themed ones.
_why_the_int: Four vocabularies spell World 5 in this codebase — map id 'futuristic_overworld', audio manifest key 'digital', a procedural cache key 'futuristic', and a monster-id suffix. Keying on an integer has no spelling to lose. The strings below are LABELS for humans editing this file; 'worlds' is the only place an int meets a word, so a rename is one line here and nowhere else. Read this mapping from this file rather than copying it into a GDScript const — a second copy is the hand-maintained duplicate that drifts.
_guard: Assert set(worlds.keys()) == {1,2,3,4,5,6} and that every job carries every label. SET EQUALITY, not 'contains' and not per-key iteration — a per-key loop passes a file that is missing World 5 entirely. ⚠️ One level up, _get_world_for_map() is a prefix chain whose miss case is 'return 1', so an unmatched map and a genuine World 1 map are the same observation; a new W3 village whose id starts with neither 'steampunk_' nor 'brasston' gets medieval names silently.
_scope: Starter jobs only (5 of 15). The 9 advanced/meta jobs are debug-gated and deliberately absent — absence must hit an EXPLICIT 'use the base name from jobs.json' branch, not a lookup that happens to miss. Ask before authoring the other 54 cells; that is a lot of speculative content behind a debug gate.
